title: A guard lane proves its Windows guard tests before hand-off
why: Lane lint runs no Windows guard tests, so a guard change can pass every lane check and go red only in batch CI. Incident: #2379 in batch 78 (PR 2583, 2026-11-11 06:37 CST), job checks-windows-guard, the linked-nm `cd "$R"` case: allow where deny was wanted. Harm: one dropped lane and one wasted batch run per miss.
source: coordinator 2026-11-11 06:43 CST (stage 3; file only, no build under the freeze)
note: Ruling R26 (owner, relayed 10:02 CST Nov 11, plan 258b86a) folds this into plan item 3.5: a lane's own checks run the Windows slice, touched-file mutation tests and signed-commit cases. Lane code-guard-3 started 07:29 CST Nov 12 (coordinator fan-out, Sonnet, medium). 05:00 CST Nov 13, coordinator: three batches went red on lane failures that the lane's own checks did not catch. #3115 failed on #3079 (Windows), #3118 on #2978 (Windows), and #3107 on #2978 (Linux). Each red costs a full batch run and a rebuild. Proposed new step windows-proof-before-handin; not filed, because this step and two others cover it. Correction to the lanes' premise: a draft PR does run checks. .github/workflows/lane-touched-tests.yml on main (step windows-tests-for-touched-files, done; item 400 a) runs the test files a draft touches, on Windows and macOS. The likely gap is suites that read a changed file but are not touched by the diff, which step lane-lint-hook-suites (#3104) addresses on Linux. Its Windows side is this step. Before building, the lane checks which tests failed in those three runs, and whether each was touched by its lane.
